name: chem-mc-postrun-r2
context:
THE POST-RUN AUDIT. The Monte Carlo engineering run was approved by you before compute was spent; this is the result. 32 cells, resolution VI, six factors, 30 seeds per cell, 29 minutes. No cell was dropped and no threshold was moved.

─────────── THE HEADLINE: ZERO OF 32 CELLS CLEARED THE PRE-REGISTERED BAR ───────────

AGENCY FLOOR, the gate that was failing at 4.1% before the run, IS SOLVABLE. Best cell 25.5%, clearing the 25% requirement. Four cells reached 23-26%.

SEED SHARE IS NOT. Required <= 35%. Best cell 52%. Range across all 32 cells: 52% to 72%. Every single acceptance failure was seed share, and no combination of six factors moved it below 52%.

So the run answered its question and the answer was no.

─────────── MAIN EFFECTS, LENTH'S PSEUDO STANDARD ERROR ───────────

AGENCY FLOOR %, noise floor +/-1.4:

    PREVIEW     +31.6   SIGNIFICANT -- dominant, and larger than everything else combined
    OPTIONS      +4.6   SIGNIFICANT
    POOL         +4.2   SIGNIFICANT
    TOPOLOGY     +1.4   at the noise floor
    TURNS        +1.0   not significant
    SWAP         -0.1   not significant

    interactions:  TOPOLOGYxOPTIONS -10.2, TOPOLOGYxPREVIEW -5.9, POOLxOPTIONS -4.9

SEED SHARE %, lower better:

    OPTIONS      -7.5   SIGNIFICANT, the best lever and not nearly enough
    TOPOLOGY     -3.9   SIGNIFICANT
    TURNS        +3.9   SIGNIFICANT, worse
    POOL         +2.9   SIGNIFICANT, worse
    PREVIEW      -0.0
    SWAP         -0.0

DECISION DENSITY %, the metric you required against complexity-mistaken-for-depth:

    SWAP         +9.4   SIGNIFICANT and the largest effect on this response
    TURNS        +3.2
    OPTIONS      +2.9
    POOL         +1.1

THROUGHPUT: OPTIONS +1.2 SIGNIFICANT. Three options 4.78, one option 3.54.

─────────── FOUR THINGS THE RUN ESTABLISHED ───────────

1. THE PRODUCT CHOICE IS NOT FALSIFIED. The plan declared in advance that a winner requiring OPTIONS=1 would falsify the design this whole game rests on. OPTIONS=3 is significant and positive on agency (+4.6), on throughput (+1.2, a 35% lift) and on seed share (-7.5, the best lever there). The mechanic the engine was deleting earns its place on all three.

2. SWAP IS COMPLEXITY WITHOUT DEPTH, MEASURED. Agency effect -0.1, inside the noise floor. Decision density effect +9.4, the largest on that response. It manufactures decisions and none of them are worth anything. This is exactly the failure you named -- "increasing cognitive load without increasing decision density" -- except the measurement says something sharper: it increases decision density AND NOT AGENCY, so the decisions are real and worthless. The parsimony rule discards it.

3. THE HEX BOARD IS NOT THE IMPROVEMENT IT LOOKS LIKE. TOPOLOGY main effect on agency is +1.4, exactly at the noise floor. It helps seed share (-3.9) and throughput (+0.5) slightly. But TOPOLOGYxOPTIONS is -10.2, the largest interaction in the run: hex and the product choice are worse together than either alone. The user asked for a hex grid; the measurement says it is roughly neutral and actively fights the game's core mechanic.

4. PREVIEW IS THE WHOLE STORY FOR AGENCY. +31.6 against a noise floor of 1.4. Every cell with preview high has a non-negative agency floor; every cell without it is negative. A planner cannot plan toward orders it cannot see, and no other factor substitutes.

─────────── WHAT I DID NOT DECLARE ABANDONMENT ON, AND WHY ───────────

The pre-registered abandonment criterion reads: "SEED SHARE cannot be brought under 45% by any pool or board-generation factor, which would mean the deal decides the game."

I have not triggered it, because THE ONE FACTOR LEVEL BUILT TO ATTACK SEED SHARE WAS NEVER SCREENED. POOL entered the design as RARE5 against BULK. ADAPTIVE -- orders drawn against the board's own atom inventory, so every deal carries comparable reachable orders -- is implemented and was dropped when the factor's high level was replaced mid-run. Declaring the criterion met on a pool factor that omits the pool mode designed for it would be abandoning on an untested premise. A focused stage 2 over POOL x TOPOLOGY x OPTIONS with ADAPTIVE included is running.

─────────── AND A NUMBER I AM SUSPICIOUS OF ───────────

Seed share sits between 52% and 72% on every cell, which is a narrow band for six factors crossed six ways. Farkle's is 3.3%. I imported the 35% threshold from Farkle without asking whether it transfers, and there is a structural reason it might not: Farkle scores in the thousands while this game scores 0 to 8 as small integers, so a single order landing or not landing moves a whole seed's mean by 10-20%. That is not proof the threshold is wrong, and the pre-registration forbids me moving it after seeing results. But it is the question I would want asked before this game is abandoned on that gate.

═══════════ REVISED AFTER THE ROUND-ONE POST-RUN AUDIT ═══════════

Both REVISE findings were testable and both were tested. Neither threshold was moved.

FINDING 1 -- "YOU ARE TRYING TO MEASURE A LIQUID WITH A RULER." SETTLED BY A NULL MODEL.

The permutation control: shuffle which seed each result is attributed to, independently per agent. That destroys the seed effect while leaving every marginal distribution exactly as observed -- same scores, same agents, same granularity. Whatever seed share survives is manufactured by the measurement.

    observed 47.8%   null floor 19.5%   (95th percentile 22.3%)   EXCESS 28.4 points

So the audit was RIGHT IN DIRECTION AND WRONG IN DEGREE. Roughly 20 of the 52 observed points are the ruler rather than the liquid, which is a large correction and does not reach the whole way: the seed still explains 28 points that shuffling destroys. The bar was measuring two things at once and the null separates them. Re-specifying the gate is a human decision under standing instruction 7 and has not been made here.

FINDING 2 -- "IF PREVIEW MAKES THE GAME SOLVABLE, IT ISN'T INCREASING AGENCY, IT'S DELETING THE GAME." CONFIRMED.

Tested against SOLVER MARGIN, which the agency floor does not contain:

    preview 0    agency -21.7%    solver margin 61.4%    plan at 62.8% of ceiling
    preview 5    agency  +9.9%    solver margin 14.4%    plan at 87.7% of ceiling

PREVIEW BUYS 31.6 POINTS OF AGENCY BY SPENDING 47 POINTS OF SOLVER MARGIN. It creates no skill. It converts unreachable ceiling into reachable skill and moves the player up against it. Agency and solver margin trade close to one for one, and a single gate cannot see that -- only the pair can.

═══════════ STAGE 2, AND THE ABANDONMENT CRITERION IS NOW PROPERLY TESTABLE ═══════════

I declined to abandon on stage 1 because ADAPTIVE -- the pool mode built specifically to attack seed share, drawing orders against the board's own atom inventory -- had been dropped from the screen when the POOL factor's high level was replaced mid-run. You agreed that was a legitimate defence rather than an excuse. Twelve cells, POOL x TOPOLOGY x OPTIONS, preview 5, 40 seeds:

    pool      topo    opt |  read   plan   ceil | agency   seed%   throughput
    RARE5     SQ        3 |  4.60   5.05   6.13 |   9.8%   50.5%    4.60
    RARE5     HEX       3 |  4.90   5.35   5.53 |   9.2%   52.3%    4.90
    BULK      HEX       1 |  3.00   3.58   4.22 |  19.2%   61.1%    3.00
    ADAPTIVE  SQ        3 | 38.23  37.58  44.65 |  -1.7%   42.8%   38.23
    ADAPTIVE  HEX       3 | 42.00  39.55  54.52 |  -5.8%   39.0%   42.00

ADAPTIVE REACHES THE BEST SEED SHARE IN THE WHOLE STUDY, 39.0%, AND IT IS DEGENERATE. Throughput 29 to 42 against a pre-registered band of 2 to 8. Diagnosed rather than inferred: its pool averages 15.6 of the 16 library molecules, and 79.3% of pool molecules are ALREADY ON THE BOARD when issued. An order already sitting there ships the instant it is issued, its replacement is drawn from the same near-complete pool, and the book cascades. Agency goes NEGATIVE at three options (-1.7%, -5.8%), which is what a trivial game looks like.

So it lowers seed share by making the game trivial, not by making the deal fairer. Among configurations inside the legitimate throughput band, THE SEED-SHARE FLOOR IS 50.5%.

═══════════ THE RESULT, STATED WITHOUT SOFTENING ═══════════

  · zero of 44 cells across both stages cleared the pre-registered bar;
  · AGENCY FLOOR is reachable -- 25.5% best, clearing its 25% requirement -- but
    only by spending solver margin, so it is not new skill;
  · SEED SHARE never goes below 50.5% in any non-degenerate configuration,
    against a bar of 35% and an abandonment criterion of 45%;
  · about 20 points of that is the metric's own floor at this score granularity,
    leaving roughly 30 points genuinely attributable to the deal;
  · the PRODUCT CHOICE is validated on three independent responses and is the one
    part of the design the run did not threaten;
  · SWAP is discarded: -0.1 agency, +9.4 decision density, real decisions worth
    nothing;
  · the HEX BOARD is neutral at best and fights the product choice, -10.2.

questions.text: The abandonment criterion said seed share under 45% by any pool or board-generation factor. ADAPTIVE reached 39% but only by making the game trivial (throughput 29-42 against a band of 2-8). Is the criterion met or not met, and does 'it got there degenerately' count as reaching it?

Preview converts solver margin into agency roughly one for one. Is that a property of THIS game, or have I discovered something that would be true of any game where the gate is defined as planner-over-readable-rule?
About 20 of the 52 points of seed share are the metric's own floor. Knowing that, what is the honest one-sentence statement to a non-technical stakeholder about whether the deal decides this game?

What should I actually ship: the square board with three product options, preview off, no swap verb — accepting a recognition game with modest planning depth? Or does the run say this design should not ship at all?
Judge the whole exercise. Was the Monte Carlo engineering run worth what it cost, and what did it establish that a smaller effort would not have?
